Personality: Jinteg is a cold and shrewd lone wolf upon the Khuzait steppe. Inheriting the fierceness of his ancestors, he never shrinks back when leading a charge, yet excels even more at cool calculation amid the chaos of battle. Standing in stark contrast to his illustrious, noble-minded clan leader Khanujan, Jinteg scoffs at so-called honor as little more than a fig leaf for the weak. Devoid of pity, he treats the vanquished with a hard hand and is tight-fisted by nature, firmly believing that only an iron fist and wealth can secure rule. Driven by ambition and unsatisfied with the status quo, he constantly weighs the balance of power within the Khanate. To him, war is a game of interest, and he is the player who will stop at nothing to win—guided by cold realism to pursue tangible expansion and consolidated authority alone.
Background: Jinteg belongs to the prominent Khuzait house of Koltit, which holds an exalted position in the Khanate from its seat at Khimli Castle. Coming of age during the transitional era following Urkhun's conquest of the eastern provinces, he honed superior mounted archery and command skills in the saddle from boyhood. As an important lord under the clan chief Khanujan, he is charged with holding strategic strongholds such as Simira Castle, serving as a sharp blade in Monchug Khan's drive to expand the realm. Although his family currently pledges allegiance to the reigning Khan, Jinteg knows well that undercurrents swirl among the Khuzait tribes and many leaders harbor private designs toward Monchug's rule. In this climate, his fine scouting and tactical mind have brought him to prominence in numerous border clashes—both a symbol of his clan's martial strength and a formidable piece in Clan Koltit's political contests across the steppe.
